newsitem.title: MEXICO: Banco de Mexico net reserves fall, assets rise.
newsitem.headline: Banco de Mexico net reserves fall, assets rise.

text.p: Banco de Mexico said on Tuesday its international reserves as of Aug. 1 were $22.485 billion compared to $22.512 billion on July 25.
The central bank said that its net international assets as of the same date were $15.360 billion compared to $15.184 billion the week before.
The central bank said the increase of $176 million in net international assets during the period was due to:
--Net income from operations by the state oil company Pemex worth $195 million.
--Net outflows of 49 million for operations with the federal government.

--A net gain of $30 million for a combination of factors including changes in the dollar value of non-dollar assets and liabilities held by the bank; net returns on interest rates and from trading of metals and securities; and net deposits in dollar accounts from commercial banks at the central bank.
The following tables detail Banco de Mexico's reserves and net domestic credit. All figures are in billions of pesos, unless otherwise indicated.
*Net International Assets are defined as gross international assets minus central bank liabilities with the IMF and assets of less than a six-month duration from other central banks.
